issues.legal_issue: An eviction decree is mandatory when monthly rent is undisputed as to its standard amount, remains in substantial arrears, and the tenant fails to pay within the period following a written demand notice.
material_facts: The landlord sued to recover possession on, among other grounds, the tenants’ failure to pay rent.
Rent was payable monthly, and the claimed arrears covered more than six months.
The landlord served a written notice demanding the arrears, but the tenants did not pay within the period following the notice.
The tenants did not raise a dispute about the amount of standard rent or permitted increases.

The tenants asserted that the landlord had not provided receipts and had demanded compensation for use and occupation; the courts below nevertheless found neglect to pay, and the Supreme Court upheld their decision.
issues.conclusion: The statutory conditions for eviction were met, so the courts were bound to pass and uphold the eviction decree; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 12(2) and 12(3)(a) of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947, where rent is payable monthly, there is no dispute about standard rent or permitted increases, the rent is in arrears for six months or more, and the tenant neglects to pay within one month after the written demand notice, the court shall pass a decree for eviction. The 1963 amendment replaced “may pass” with “shall pass,” making the decree mandatory when those conditions are satisfied. Harbanslal Jagmohandas & Anr. v. Prabhudas Shivlal, [1976] 3 SCR 628, was relied on in applying Section 12(3)(a). Mohan Laxman Hede v. Noormohamed Adam Shaikh, AIR 1988 SC 1111, was distinguished because it concerned regular deposits under Section 12(3)(b), not total failure or neglect to pay under clause (a).

rule.if: possession_suit_for_unpaid_rent and rent_payable_monthly and no_standard_rent_dispute and arrears_for_six_months_or_more and tenant_did_not_pay_after_notice

predicates.possession_suit_for_unpaid_rent: A landlord brought a suit seeking possession on the ground that rent was unpaid.
predicates.rent_payable_monthly: The rent was payable from month to month.
predicates.no_standard_rent_dispute: The tenant did not dispute the amount of standard rent or permitted increases.
predicates.arrears_for_six_months_or_more: The rent or permitted increases remained unpaid for at least six months.
predicates.tenant_did_not_pay_after_notice: The tenant failed to pay the demanded rent within the period following the landlord’s written notice.

issues.definition: When a landlord’s possession suit concerns unpaid rent, the rent is payable monthly, its standard amount is undisputed, substantial arrears have accumulated, and the tenant does not pay after notice, an eviction decree must be passed.
